source: BIS residential property prices (WS_SPP bulk CSV) — REAL data, committed at pipeline/data/bis_property.json
license: BIS data are free to download and use (BIS terms and conditions); no key, no account — see pipeline/acquire_bis.py
entity_kind: economy (BIS 2-letter code), e.g. US, DE, JP

time_range.time_id: feature (as-of) year; annual value = mean of the year's observed quarters of the 2010=100 index

features: 18-dim economy-year vector, 5 masked families ['level', 'momentum', 'vol', 'cycle', 'gap'] — the exact committed pipeline/build_features.py construction (parity-checked bit-identical). X = MaskedZScaler output with the scaler fit on train rows (feature-year <= 2009) ONLY; X_raw = unscaled with NaN at unobserved cells; M = observability mask. Features for row (economy, t) use quarters <= t only.

next_year_price_change.construction: y = 100*(a[t+1]/a[t] - 1) on the REAL (inflation-adjusted) annual index of the same economy — strictly forward data. Windows ending after 2025 excluded (2026 is a partial year in the committed snapshot).

three_year_price_change.construction: y = 100*(a[t+3]/a[t] - 1), cumulative REAL change over (t, t+3]. Same exclusion rule for windows past 2025.

above_market_appreciation.construction: y = 1 if next-year REAL change > that feature-year's cross-economy cohort median (cohort = economies with a defined next-year label at year t; years with <5 labeled economies skipped). The median uses only data from (t, t+1] — strictly forward of features — and never crosses the temporal split boundary: train-year medians (label-end <= 2015) are functions of train-period outcomes only; test-year medians of test-period outcomes only. Medians are label definitions, never model inputs. This follows the registry's 'beats the cross-sectional median' semantics; under a temporal (not entity) split the cohort at each year IS the training universe of economies, so no per-year median can be computed from a disjoint entity set.

split.harness: per-target time_key = label-END year, cut = 2016 (train: label ends <= 2015; test: label ends >= 2016) — the registry's 'train target-year <= 2015, test after'. Baselines fit on each target's full train side.
split.mtnn: train = feature-year <= 2009 (1280 rows), val = 2010-2012 (177 rows, early stopping only), test-side = feature-year >= 2013 (818 rows, never seen at fit time). t = 2012 is the latest feature year whose 3-year label window ends inside the global train period (2015), so the MTNN never forward-passes any row that is a harness test row for ANY target. This makes the MTNN's supervised universe a strict subset of what baselines see on the 1y targets (baselines fit through feature-year 2014) — a disclosed handicap, not an advantage.

leakage_note: Labels are strictly forward-shifted: the label for (economy, t) uses only annual real-index values at years > t; features use quarters <= t. Label windows never span the split cut (split is on label-END year). Feature scaling is fit on MTNN-train rows only. The above-market cohort median is part of the label definition, computed within each label window, never fed to any model.
